## Lecture 5: Exposure variability

------------------------------------------------------------------------

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Click to view catchup R code"

# set your working directory with `setwd()`!!

# load packages we need
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)

# read dataset excel file and make sure it's a tibble
ehs655 <- read_xlsx("Dataset V1.xlsx") %>% as_tibble()

# clean job title variable to remove misspellings
ehs655 <- ehs655 %>%
  mutate(
    `Job-title` = 
      case_when(
        `Job-title` == "Lborer" ~ "Laborer",
        `Job-title` == "Laboerr" ~ "Laborer",
        `Job-title` == "Electrican" ~ "Electrician",
        `Job-title` == "Carpentr" ~ "Carpenter",
        `Job-title` == "Operaing engineer" ~ "Operating engineer",
        `Job-title` == "Ironworkr" ~ "Ironworker",
        `Job-title` == "" ~ NA,
        .default = `Job-title`))

# convert LEQ values <LOD to LOD/sqrt(2)
ehs655 <- ehs655 %>%
  mutate(`Work-LEQ-dBA` = ifelse(`Work-LEQ-dBA` < 70, 70/sqrt(2), `Work-LEQ-dBA`))
```
:::

### Dimensions of exposure variability

- Fundamental dimensions

  - Person

  - Time

  - Space

- Other contributing factors

  - Measurement method Is variability in exposure desirable or undesirable?

- Is it better to make…

  - More measurements on few individuals?

  - Fewer/one measurement on many individuals?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Basic concepts

- If exposures [varied over time, but not among people]{.underline}, we could…

  - Monitor single individual continuously

  - Make multiple measurements randomly distributed over time on that individual

- If exposures varied [between people, but not over time]{.underline}, we could…

  - Make single instantaneous measure on every person

  - More people better; repeated measurements not

### Temporal variability

- Basic dimension of variability at individual level

  - Change jobs or residence

  - Quit smoking

  - Retire

- Exposures vary within and between days, months, years, decades

- Congenital attributes may be only exposure truly fixed at individual level

  - However, many epidemiological methods require exposures to be treated as fixed (e.g., case-control)

### Measures to summarize exposure variability

- Continuous data

  - Standard deviation ($\sigma$)

  - Variance ($\sigma^2$)

  - Interquartile range

- Categorical data

  - Frequency table

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Another measure to describe variability

Standard error of the mean

$$
SE(\bar{x})=\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}
$$

How does this differ from the standard deviation?

- **SD is measure of dispersion** of data around mean

- SD stays the same (on average) when sample size increases

- **SE describes accuracy of sample mean** as estimate of population mean

- SE decreases with increasing sample size

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data manipulation functions in R

**Rename variable:**

```{r, eval=FALSE}
rename(new_varname = old_varname)
```

**Generate a new variable:**

```{r, eval=FALSE}
mutate(new_var = *some manipulation to old_var*)
```

**Replace an existing variable**

```{r, eval=FALSE}
mutate(old_var = *some manipulation to old_var*)
```

- **E.g., convert variable to string/character**

  ```{r, eval=FALSE}
  mutate(old_var = as.character(old_var))
  ```

<!-- -->

- **E.g., assign labels to categorical data**

  ```{r, eval=FALSE}
  mutate(old_var = factor(old_var, 
                          labels = c("label1", "label2", ..., "labelN")))
  ```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data manipulation functions in R

**Logical operators are very powerful**

- i.e., `&` and `|`

- R has `%in%` operator to see if an element belongs to a vector

  ```{r}
  c(1, 2, 3) %in% c(1, 2)
  ```

- See more at <https://www.w3schools.com/r/r_operators.asp>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data manipulation functions in R

**Replace existing value**

```{r, eval = FALSE}
mutate(
  var =
    case_when(
      condition_1 ~ "value_if_true_1",
      condition_2 ~ "value_if_true_2",
      TRUE ~ "default_value"  # Acts as the "ELSE" statement
    )
)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data manipulation functions in R

**Create dummy variables for groups**

```{r, eval = FALSE}
mutate(dummy_var = ifelse(old_var > 70, 1, 0))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Making a fancier ggplot in R

Fancier version of a boxplot with labels, different aesthetics, flipping the axes, and theme

```{r}
ehs655 %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = `Job-title`, y = `Work-LEQ-dBA`),
               outlier.shape = 1, outlier.fill = "transparent",
               color = "black", fill = "#f7fafc",
               linewidth = 0.3, width = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "LEQ noise levels (dBA) by job title",
       x = "Job title", 
       y = "LEQ (dBA) noise level") +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_flip()
```
